questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Union
questions.problem: If $\overset{―}{X}={2.1,\pi ,\sqrt{7},11}$ and $\overset{―}{Y}={2,\pi ,11},$ then what is $\overset{―}{X\cup Y}?$
questions.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for unions states that

$$
\overset{―}{X\cup Y}≡\overset{―}{X}\cap \overset{―}{Y}.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X\cup Y} & =\overset{―}{X}\cap \overset{―}{Y} \\  & ={2.1,\pi ,\sqrt{7},11}\cap {2,\pi ,11} \\  & ={\pi ,11}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Union
canonical_examples.problem: If $\overline{X} = \{ a, c, d\}$ and $\overline{Y} = \{ a, e, i, o, u \},$ then what is $\overline{ X \cup Y }?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for unions states that

$$
\overline{X \cup Y} \equiv \overline{X} \cap \overline{Y}.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X\cup Y} & =\overset{―}{X}\cap \overset{―}{Y} \\  & ={a,c,d}\cap {a,e,i,o,u} \\  & ={a}.\end{aligned}
$$

De Morgan's law for intersections states that

$$

$$
